title: Kurmanzhan Datka
summary: Kurmanzhan Datka (1811–1907) became datka, a governor of Alai Kyrgyz tribes, after her husband Alymbek Datka was assassinated; Aramco World dates this to 1865. Kokand, Bukhara and Russia all recognised her authority, and the Russians styled her queen of the Alai. Her youngest son Kamchybek was hanged by Russian forces in 1895. Her base was at Gulcha, and she is buried in Osh.

uncertainty.note: Both RFE/RL and Aramco World give 1811; Aramco World says she held the title until her death at age 97 and was photographed in 1906 "when she was about 95". 1907 is the end of the RFE/RL range.

as_recorded.value: Kamchybek, was hanged by Russian forces in 1895

where.modern_name: Gulcha, Alay District, Osh Region, Kyrgyzstan (pinned to her headquarters, the de facto capital of the Alai region she ruled; she is buried in Osh)
where.historical_name: Gulcha in the Alai Valley, under the Khanate of Kokand until its absorption into the Russian Empire (Turkestan) in the 1870s

importance.justification: Both sources describe her as a female ruler of the Alai whose authority was recognised by Kokand, Bukhara and Russia, remembered as a national figure in Kyrgyzstan.

sources.title: Qishloq Ovozi: Who Was Kurmanjan Datka?
Kurmanjan-Datka and Russian generals: assessment of its activities and awards

reviewer_note: RFE/RL notes she helped persuade other Kyrgyz to live under Russian rule; the summary reports only that Russia styled her queen of the Alai. The 1865 date is Aramco World only and her death year is inferred from the RFE/RL range. Osh State University abstract confirms the youngest son was executed (no year).
